newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cardoso signs bill to cut tax, spur growth.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cardoso signs bill to cut tax, spur growth.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed a bill exempting exports, capital goods and electrical power used in the manufacturing process from an ICMS tax on the sale and circulation of goods and services.
The bill is expected to boost annual gross domestic product by 1.5 percent and Cardoso hailed it as the most important tax cut in Brazil in recent decades.
The bill is expected to come into effect Monday when it is due to be published in Brazil's Official Gazette.

Exports and power will be exempted from the tax immediately while imports of capital goods will be free of the tax from November 1. From January 1, 1998, other goods used in the manufacturing process will also be ICMS-free.

The federal government will compensate Brazil's state governments who levy the ICMS tax by issuing them with a corresponding amount of National Treasury debt paper which they may use towards reducing debts with the central government.

Cardoso said the bill represented a major element of the tax reform his government has been preparing to push through Congress. He also predicted its pension and administrative reforms would be approved by the end of the year.
